investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) cannot be satisfied.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, all 6 nodes fail. A recent node label change or cluster resize could have reduced the eligible node count.

Peer-pod VM quota limit at the infrastructure or cloud provider level: the underlying VM quota for the kata.peerpods.io runtime class may be capped at a value that is now fully consumed, preventing the Kubernetes resource from being replenished even after pods terminate.

Leaked remote agent VMs not releasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their peer-pod VMs (e.g., due to a crash in the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs), the resource counter on those 2 nodes would remain depleted.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.
If the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are found to be in a NotReady or cordoned state, the root cause would be node unavailability rather than resource exhaustion.
If no pending or running remote-agent pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the resource counter may be incorrect due to a peer-pod controller bug rather than actual VM consumption.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed to exclude more nodes (reducing the eligible pool below 2), that configuration change would be the primary cause rather than resource exhaustion on the existing 2 nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes and warns before the resource is fully exhausted (e.g., warn at 80% utilization, fail at 100%).

Add a node eligibility eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting if the eligible node pool shrinks unexpectedly.
Add a preemption-readiness eval that verifies at least one preemption victim exists for remote agent pods, so scheduling failures due to non-preemptible workloads are caught proactively.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented agent creation entirely, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out unscheduled (~121–154 s across all three checks), so no agent is ever created, no state is ever polled, and the eval evidence object remains empty. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agents VM node pool; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader production outage is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) cannot be satisfied.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, all 6 nodes fail. A recent node label change or cluster resize could have reduced the eligible node count.

Peer-pod VM quota limit at the infrastructure or cloud provider level: the underlying VM quota for the kata.peerpods.io runtime class may be capped at a value that is now fully consumed, preventing the Kubernetes resource from being replenished even after pods terminate.

Leaked remote agent VMs not releasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their peer-pod VMs (e.g., due to a crash in the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs), the resource counter on those 2 nodes would remain depleted.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are shown to also carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the affinity rules are intentionally correct, the capacity problem is strictly limited to the 2 eligible nodes and the affinity configuration is not a contributing factor.
If historical eval runs (once history is available) show this check has never passed, the issue may be a configuration or provisioning problem rather than a regression.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node, alerting before slots are fully exhausted rather than only after a pod fails to schedule.

Add a stuck-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) to catch cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 3), alerting if the eligible node count drops to a level that makes the feature fragile under normal load.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run check (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) as an early step in the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish scheduling failures from API or runtime failures before the full latency budget is consumed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM never started and the runtime response contract could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never produced an agent, and the expected-output contract fields orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message were never populated. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, possibly because node labels changed or the pod spec targets a node group that no longer has sufficient members.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 of 6) may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any live workload, causing transient or sustained exhaustion.
Lower probability — eval runner submitting pods with an overly restrictive node selector that excludes nodes which could otherwise host kata peer-pods, if the selector was recently tightened.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether capacity is fully consumed by live workloads, leaked pods, or prior eval runs that did not clean up via withCleanup.
List all pods across all namespaces that are requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm resources; terminate any that are stale, orphaned, or from failed eval runs to free slots.

Investigate why 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector — review current node labels and compare against the pod spec's affinity rules to determine if label drift has reduced the schedulable pool.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by live workload, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool needs to be scaled out (additional nodes or increased VM slot limits per node) to accommodate both production workload and eval probes.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it reliably releases VM slots after each eval run, including on failure paths, to prevent slot leakage across runs.

Because verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, confirm whether this eval has ever passed in this environment; if not, validate the cluster configuration before treating this as a regression.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded only due to a node label that was recently removed or changed, the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to node affinity/selector misconfiguration.

If the eval runner is found to be submitting pods with an incorrect or overly restrictive node selector not present in prior passing runs, the cause would be a runner configuration change rather than infrastructure capacity.
If no prior passing run exists (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null), the failure may reflect a never-validated environment rather than a regression.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing exhaustion before a pod is submitted.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 1 node with available VM slots), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods from prior eval runs remain Running or Pending after the withCleanup phase completes.
Add a historical trend eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over time to detect gradual exhaustion before it reaches 100%.
